findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached endpoint VJP derivative path, so no affinity-head gradient or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed score window is [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing, and the curve support is [0.0, 0.49]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity target is observable in the supplied evidence.

Continuous contrast features are represented in predicted endpoint world coordinates and are fit by observed-node linear interpolation with extrapolation disallowed; polynomial fits are not accepted for the inspected rows, so time-conditioned rules must stay inside the observed support.

Inspected landmark_00 contrast features show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts within the window (e.g. 4-10 sign changes and 1-9 strong sign conflicts across the six inspected rows), and first-rate versus last-rate z values frequently reverse sign, which is inconsistent with a single constant-direction rule over the whole window.

Whole-window z values for the inspected landmark_00 features are small relative to their first/last rate z values (whole-window z between about -0.58 and 0.64), so the integrated window contrast is weak even where local rates are large; point-estimate ranking of local rates alone would overstate support.

hypotheses.falsifier: A constant-direction rule matching or exceeding the observed-node fit fidelity of the time-conditioned rule on held-out observed nodes.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00 local contrast features over observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule that follows the observed-node sign of landmark_00 local contrast features will track the observed window better than a constant-direction rule, because the inspected features change sign multiple times inside the observed support.

hypotheses.direction: uncertainty-adjusted ranking differs from point-estimate ranking
hypotheses.falsifier: Uncertainty-adjusted and point-estimate rankings coincide for all inspected features.
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z versus first/last rate z for the same feature
hypotheses.statement: Ranking coordinate hypotheses by uncertainty and multiplicity-adjusted support will reorder priorities relative to ranking by point-estimate magnitude, because whole-window z values are small while local rate z values are large for the same features.

limitations: Recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity benefit or final-affinity comparison can be established from the supplied evidence.

Only six continuous_trends rows were inspected; the remaining rows, and the branch_adjusted, endpoint_effects, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, survival_effects and turnover_accounting tables, were not read in this turn.
No decoded terminal labels, descendant survival credit or turnover residual were read, so selection enrichment cannot be distinguished from absolute geometric descriptors here.
Contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies, and no neural-module causation is claimed.
